1000300010301: You came over the obsidian bridge? Then you were lucky.
Death Knights patrol that bridge now. They charge a toll in blood from anyone crossing.
No trader has made it across in weeks, and the camp is running out of everything.
Break their patrol. Ten fallen knights should reopen the road.
They ride in pairs along the bridge. Come back when %count% have fallen.
Have %count% %name%s fallen yet? Still no traders on the bridge.
A wagon crossed the bridge this morning! The road is open again.
Tell them the toll's been paid.
1000300010302: Nothing grows on this mountain except my fire pumpkins. They love the hot ash.
But the Eyes have found them. They float down at night and swallow them whole.
They glow brighter after every one. I think the fire inside the pumpkins feeds them.
Get me back five pumpkins, before I've got nothing left to plant next season.
The Eyes that glow brightest have eaten the most. I need %count% pumpkins.
Do you have the %count% %name%s yet? My patch is nearly bare.
Five pumpkins, still warm inside! I'll save the seeds this time.
Maybe build a roof over the patch.
1000300010401: Don't climb any higher without covering your eyes.
The Eyes near the summit stare so hot it burns. Three climbers came back blind with fever this month.
The healers can't keep up, and the summit shrine is cut off.
Bring down ten of them, and maybe the pilgrims can climb again.
Strike fast and don't meet their gaze. Come back after %count%.
Have %count% %name%s been put out yet? Another climber came down burning.
The pilgrims are climbing again. You did what our healers couldn't.
1000300010402: I'm brewing a cooling draught that lets you walk through flame unharmed.
The only thing that makes it work is ash mushrooms. They grow inside old armour, in the heat and dark.
And the only old armour on this mountain is being worn by Death Knights.
So you want me to pick mushrooms off a Death Knight?
Off five of them, yes. Bring me the mushrooms and I'll name the draught after you.
Look in the gaps of their armour. I need %count% clumps.
Do you have the %count% clumps of %name% yet? My cauldron is waiting.
Perfect, grey and smoking! The draught will be ready by morning.
Please don't name it after me.
1000400010301: There's a tomb under these dunes, and something is guarding it.
Skeletons with bones like iron. They were the king's own guard, buried standing up around his tomb.
Now they've marched out, and they cut down anyone who comes near the dunes.
Break ten of them. Their bones are tough, but they're not unbreakable.
Bring a heavy weapon. Come back when %count% of them are in pieces.
Have %count% %name%s been broken yet? I can hear them standing guard.
Ten of the king's guard in pieces! The dunes might finally be safe to cross.
My arms will be sore for a week.
1000400010302: The lost caravan's guards each wore a bronze helmet with their family crest on it.
The families still live in the town. They've never had anything to bury.
The skeletons walking the old road are still wearing those helmets.
So the helmets could finally go home.
That's right. Bring me five, and five families can finally lay their dead to rest.
Look for the crests on the brow. I need %count% helmets.
Do you have the %count% %name%s yet? The families keep asking me.
Five helmets, crests still clear. Five families will light candles tonight.
I'm glad I could help them.
1000400010401: Ever since the Ogres broke into the old tomb, the dead have been getting up.
Hundreds. Every night more skeletons rise around the tomb and wander toward the wells.
We can't drink, we can't sleep, and the children are too scared to go outside.
Put ten of them back down. That should buy us a few quiet nights.
They wander between the tomb and the wells. Come back after %count%.
Have %count% %name%s been put down yet? They were at the wells again last night.
The wells are clear, and the children slept through the night.
1000400010402: The tomb held burial urns with the ashes of the old desert kings.
The Ogres smashed their way in and carried the urns off to use as cooking pots.
Is that why the dead are restless?
Yes. The kings can't rest until their ashes are home, and their soldiers won't either.
Bring back five urns, and I'll return them to the tomb myself.
Please handle them with care. All %count% urns need to go home.
Do you have the %count% %name%s yet? The dead are getting angrier.
Five urns, and I don't think the ashes even spilled. The kings can rest.
Ogre stew will taste different now.
1000500010301: Stay out of the berry thickets unless you want a nasty bite.
Snakes. A warm spring brought them out early, and the bushes are full of them.
Four of our foragers have been bitten this week, and the berries are rotting on the vine.
Clear out ten snakes, and the foragers can get back to work.
Watch your ankles in the thickets. Come back when %count% are dead.
Have %count% %name%s been dealt with yet? Another forager got bitten.
The foragers are filling their baskets again. Thank you, truly.
1000500010302: I keep antivenom for snakebites, in little vials drying on a rack by the cave.
Last night the bats swooped down and carried off every shiny vial on the rack.
Yes, and with this many snakes about, someone will need it before long.
Knock down the bats and bring me back five vials. Lives depend on it.
The bats roost by the cave mouth. Bring back %count% vials, unbroken.
Do you have the %count% %name%s yet? Another forager is limping.
Five vials, not a crack in them! The foragers are safe now.
1000500010401: The woodcutters won't use the north road any more.
Goblin raiders hide in the ferns along the road and jump out at every cart.
They've taken axes, saws and two oxen. The lumber camp is close to starving.
Hit them back. Ten raiders down, and the rest will think twice.
They hide in the ferns beside the road. Come back when %count% are down.
Have %count% %name%s been dealt with yet? Another cart was robbed.
The carts are rolling again, and nobody's been ambushed in days. Well done.
Tell them to oil their wheels.
1000500010402: When the goblins first attacked, the ranger at the watchtower ran for his life.
He dropped the tower keys in the ferns, right on top of a snake nest.
They coil round anything cold and shiny. Every snake in that nest is hoarding a key.
Bring me five keys and we can man the watchtower again.
The snakes near the tower have the keys. I need %count% of them.
Do you have the %count% %name%s yet? The tower is still dark.
Five keys! The watchtower's lantern will be lit tonight.
Tell the ranger not to run so fast next time.
1000600010301: Do you see the apple orchard behind the inn? It's crawling with snakes.
They come for the fallen apples, then for the mice that eat the apples.
Now nobody can pick fruit, and the cider press has gone quiet.
Clear out ten of them, and the harvest can go ahead.
Check under the trees with the most windfall. Come back after %count%.
Have %count% %name%s been cleared yet? The apples are going to waste.
The pickers are back in the trees! There'll be cider this year after all.
1000600010302: I'm the town tanner. Adventurers sell me monster claws, and I turn them into charms and buckles.
Rats broke into my storeroom and dragged every claw down into the drains.
What would rats want with claws?
They sharpen their teeth on them! The ones down there are getting bigger, too.
Bring me back five claws before those rats turn into monsters themselves.
The rats carry them in their teeth. I need %count% claws back.
Do you have the %count% %name%s yet? The rats are getting bolder.
Five claws, barely chewed! I can open the shop again.
1000600010401: The town archives are being eaten, one page at a time.
Rats. They've nested in the records room and chewed through a hundred years of town history.
Land deeds, birth records, the founding charter, all turned into rat nests.
Stop them, please. Ten rats should save what pages are left.
They nest behind the shelves. Come back when %count% are gone.
Have %count% %name%s been dealt with yet? I can hear paper tearing.
The archives are quiet. What's left of our history is safe.
Nice to have history that isn't eaten.
1000600010402: Under the town hall is a vault holding the shields of the town's founders.
When the spring floods came, snakes slithered in and curled up inside the shields.
They drag them off to their dens, where the shields keep them warm and dry.
Bring back five shields before the founders' day parade, or we'll have nothing to carry.
They're heavy, but the snakes hoard them in the reeds. I need %count%.
Do you have the %count% %name%s yet? The parade is coming soon.
Five founders' shields, and only a little muddy. The parade is saved!
I expect a seat at the front.
1000300010101: Careful where you step, traveller. The ground here is still warm from the last eruption.
What are those floating things over the vents?
Eyes. They drift up out of the lava with the smoke and never blink.
Whatever one of them sees, the Death Knights on the ridge know a moment later.
Our miners can't lift a pick without being hunted down. Put out ten of those Eyes for me.
Look for them where the smoke is thickest. Come back once %count% have fallen.
Have you blinded %count% %name%s yet? I can still feel them watching.
The vents are quiet. For once nothing is staring back at me.
The Death Knights just lost their scouts.
1000300010102: Something else, now that the Eyes are thinner on the ground.
Last night Death Knights rode down on our supply wagon. They took every loaf of bread we had.
The dead don't need to eat.
No, they don't. They burn it at the crater's edge to starve the living off this mountain.
Take back five loaves before they reach the fire, and my miners can keep working.
The knights carry the loaves on their saddles. Bring me %count% before they burn.
Do you have the %count% loaves of %name% yet? The miners are getting hungry.
Still warm from the lava, and not one of them burnt. You've fed the whole camp tonight.
1000300010201: Turn back now, unless you've come to fight.
Who are the knights marching down from the peak?
They were the Order of the Caldera. They swore to hold back the fire and died in it a hundred years ago.
The fire wouldn't let them rest. Now they march down every night to burn what's left of the valley.
Strike down ten of them. Every one that falls is one fewer at our gates.
They hit hard and never tire. Come back when %count% of them are ash.
Have %count% %name%s fallen yet? I can hear their armour on the ridge again.
Ten fewer blades at our gates. Maybe the fallen order can rest now.
They fought like they still had a vow to keep.
1000300010202: The old order built wardstones around the caldera to keep the lava down.
They cooled them with sap jewels, amber from the ironwood trees that hardens in the heat.
But the Eyes are drawn to anything that glitters. They've swallowed the jewels out of every stone.
Yes, they are. Cut five jewels out of the Eyes, and I can reseal the ward before the mountain wakes.
The jewels glow orange inside them. I need %count% to seal the wards.
Do you have %count% %name%s yet? The ground keeps shaking.
Still warm, and not a crack in any of them. The wardstones will hold for another age.
1000400010101: Do you hear that rattling under the sand? That isn't the wind.
A whole caravan. A sandstorm swallowed it, merchants, camels and guards, three generations ago.
Now the storms are uncovering them again, and the bones are getting up.
They keep marching the old trade route, killing anyone on it. Put ten of them back in the ground.
Follow the old road markers. Come back when %count% of them are scattered.
Have %count% %name%s been laid to rest yet? I still hear rattling at night.
The road is quiet again. Perhaps the old caravan has finally finished its journey.
1000400010102: There's a shrine at the oasis. Every dawn we pour water from five golden goblets to bless the spring.
A band of Ogres smashed their way in and carried the goblets off as drinking cups.
Can't you just use other cups?
Since the blessing stopped, the spring has dropped by a hand's width every day.
Take the goblets back from the Ogres before the oasis runs dry.
The Ogres won't hand them over. Bring me all %count% goblets, they're our lifeblood.
Do you have the %count% %name%s yet? The water gets lower every morning.
All five! I'll pour the blessing at first light, and the spring will rise again.
Could you rinse the Ogre spit off first?
1000400010201: Stay off the dune tops. The Ogres can see you for miles up there.
Ogres? This far into the desert?
A great storm drove them out of the red canyons. Now they've made their camp out here.
They smash our wells looking for water and toss our riders around like dolls.
Bring down ten of the brutes, and the rest may go back where they came from.
Aim for the knees, they're slow to turn. Come back when %count% have fallen.
Have %count% %name%s fallen yet? Another well was smashed last night.
Ten Ogres down? You hit harder than a sandstorm.
And I hold a grudge for longer.
1000400010202: Every night after the moon rises, we hear drums out in the dunes.
The old Iron Legion died out here, and their hardest dead still carry the war drums.
Every beat calls more bones up out of the sand.
So no drums, no new skeletons.
That's right. Break the Hard Skeletons, take five of their drums, and the desert can sleep again.
Follow the beat in the dark. I need %count% drums to bury in salt.
Do you have the %count% %name%s yet? The drumming was louder last night.
Five drums, and the dunes are silent. I'll bury them deep in the salt flats.
1000500010101: Listen. That chopping sound, hear it? Those are goblin axes.
The elder oaks. Each one is older than any kingdom, and the goblins are turning them into a fort.
Once that wall is up, they'll raid every village along the river.
Drive them off. Ten goblins should be enough to scatter the work gangs.
Follow the stumps. Come back when %count% goblins have fallen.
Have %count% %name%s fallen yet? I can still hear the axes.
The chopping has stopped. The elder oaks will stand a while longer, thanks to you.
1000500010102: The forest wardens keep the seeds of every rare tree locked away in iron chests.
The forest snakes here love cold metal, and they're as greedy as magpies.
Last night they slithered into my hut and swallowed the padlocks right off the chests.
Five of them, keys and all. Until I get them back, any squirrel could empty my seed vault.
The fat, slow ones are your best bet. Bring back %count% padlocks.
Do you have the %count% %name%s yet? The squirrels are watching my chests.
Five padlocks, a bit slimy but working. The seed vault is safe again.
1000500010201: Mind your neck after dusk. The Hollow caves wake up then.
Bats, thousands of them. They used to feed on moths, but now they drink sap from the elder trees.
The trees are going grey and brittle, and the forest is dying from the inside.
Thin out the swarm. Ten bats would give the trees a chance to heal.
They swarm thickest around the cave mouths. Come back when %count% are gone.
Have %count% %name%s been dealt with yet? More bark goes grey every night.
I can see green sap rising in the bark again. You've given the old trees a chance.
No more bats at the buffet.
1000500010202: White owls watch over this forest. They keep the dark things away at night.
Goblins have been snaring them and plucking their feathers for war headdresses.
Each stolen feather weakens the owls' watch over the wood.
Can feathers really be given back?
If you lay them at the owl shrine, the owls will take them back. Bring me five.
The goblin chieftains wear the most. Collect %count% feathers for the shrine.
Do you have the %count% %name%s yet? The owls have gone quiet.
Five white feathers. Listen, the owls are calling again.
I think they're saying thank you.
1000600010101: Oi, you! Got a moment? The old mill's been taken over.
Rats. They nested in the flour sacks after the miller left, and now there's a whole army of them.
They raid the bakery every night and leave nothing but crumbs and droppings.
Clear out ten of the fattest, and I can start grinding flour again.
They're thickest under the millstones. Come back when %count% are done.
Have you cleared out %count% %name%s yet? I can hear them chewing on the sacks.
The mill wheel is turning again! Bread for everyone this week.
1000600010102: The town healer grows glowcap mushrooms in the damp cellars by the canal.
They're the only cure for marsh fever, and half the town is coughing.
The snakes found out the glowcaps stay warm, so they drag them back to their nests to warm their eggs.
Too clever. Bring back five glowcaps, and the healer can brew a batch of the cure.
The mushrooms glow faintly green, you can't miss them. I need %count% of them.
Do you have the %count% %name%s yet? The coughing is getting worse.
Five glowcaps, and still glowing! The healer will have the cure brewed by nightfall.
Tell the snakes to find another heater.
1000600010201: Don't lean over the canal wall, friend. Something might grab you.
Snakes. The spring floods washed them down out of the hills, and they've taken over the canals.
The washerwomen won't go near the water, and two barges have sunk with their crews scrambling ashore.
Kill ten of them, and the canals might be safe enough to use again.
Check under the bridges, they like the shade. Come back after %count%.
Have %count% %name%s been dealt with yet? Nobody dares touch the canal.
I saw a barge go through this morning without anyone screaming. Thank you!
That's a low bar, but I'll take it.
1000600010202: I make the fireworks for the harvest festival, and I'm in real trouble.
Rats got into my workshop and dragged off my festival bombs. They think the fuses are food!
Rats carrying bombs around? Under the town?
Under the town, right next to the lamp-oil store. If one of them goes off down there...
Please, get five of them back before the whole street goes up with the fireworks.
Be gentle with them. I need all %count% back in one piece.
Do you have the %count% %name%s yet? Every time I hear a bang I panic.
All five, and nobody blown up! The harvest festival can go ahead after all.
Maybe keep them away from the rats this time.
1000600021101: Thank goodness, a fresh face! Please, you have to help us.
Rats! Hundreds of them. They came up out of the old drains under the market a week ago.
They've chewed through the grain stores, and the baker has had to shut his doors.
People are falling sick, and the guards won't go anywhere near the sewers.
Surely a few rats can't be that much trouble?
These aren't your cellar rats, friend. They're as big as dogs and twice as mean.
If you can cull ten of them, the rest might think twice about our streets.
Bless you! Start by the market wells, that's where they're thickest.
Come back to me once you've dealt with %count% of them.
Have you culled %count% %name%s yet? I can still hear them scratching in the walls.
You did it! The streets are quiet for the first time in days.
They won't be back in a hurry.
1000100000101: What do you mean where you are? Anyway I need help son.
You see, young one, my house, well, it's not quite the welcoming place it used to be.
It's overrun by rats, scurrying through every nook and cranny, making themselves right at home.
It's a bit of a mess, I'm afraid. Can you kill 10 rats for me, Sonny?
That way I can get into my home again.
